title: CLO 2025.0 - Real-time Hair Generation
description: Starting from version 2025.0, a new material type — Hair Strand — has been added in CLO. Users can directly create and view hair effects in the 3D window without rendering, thereby simplifying the workflow.
transcript:
In this video, I will introduce the actual hair growth function.  
In the previous version, users could only check the hair growth effect through V-Ray rendering.  
Since version 2025.0, the material types in the shell have been expanded to include a new material called Hair Growth Rate.  
Users can directly create and check the hair growth effect in the 3D window without rendering,  
thereby greatly simplifying the workflow.  
In addition, hair based on V-Ray rendering can only be viewed in the rendering window,  
which limits its use in external application programs.  
In contrast, the Hair Growth Rate material can be exported to USD format,  
greatly increasing compatibility with external tools.  
Currently, this function is only available on Windows systems, with support for Mac systems planned for the future.  
Let's take a look at how to set the Hair Growth Rate.  
If you want to display or hide the Hair Growth Rate material in the 3D window,  
hover the mouse over the clothing rendering option in the switch menu,  
click the icon to display the Hair Growth Rate,  
and then use the function.  
At this point, the Hair Growth Rate material will be displayed on the fabric with hair growth.  
You can check it in the 3D window in real time.  
You can also click on the Hair Growth Rate color randomly,  
assigning random colors to each Hair Growth Rate,  
making it easier to inspect the various shapes of hair growth.  
When you use fabric with Hair Growth Rate material,  
these options will be disabled and cannot be selected.  
You can control the Hair Growth Rate in the 3D window by choosing from three different options.  
Go to the main menu, open Settings,  
then open User Definition, and click the 3D option.  
In the Hair Growth Rate form, you will see three options:  
Original Hair, Plane, and Limit.  
Click each option to display the difference in the 3D window.  
Selecting Original Hair will display hair with thickness and width,  
helping to check the overall structure of the hair.  
Selecting Plane will display hair with width but no thickness,  
while Limit will display hair as a simple curve with no thickness or width.  
The selected option is the default.  
Limit shows hair as a simple curve,  
with neither thickness nor width.  
We can select Original Hair  
to get a more realistic appearance.  
Now let's see how to directly apply the Hair Growth Rate material to the costume.  
Click Fabric 1 in the Object window.  
In the Attribute Editor,  
change the material type to Hair Growth Rate.  
Use Fabric 1 for the costume fabric.  
It will immediately display the hair in the 3D window.  
You can also select various hair types from the following hair types.  
At the bottom of the Attribute Editor,  
similar to the previous hair dye type,  
you can adjust attribute details such as parameters,  
shape settings,  
and default application to set the hairstyle.  
Here we will quickly adjust some parameter values  
to demonstrate the working principle of hair settings.  
Although the Hair Growth Rate and hair dye use the same parameters  
and attribute settings,  
the distribution of these two hair types differs in the hair dye window.  
In the hair dye list,  
a new Random option has been added.  
By adjusting the seed distribution value,  
even with the same parameters,  
you can create a slightly different hair arrangement.  
After setting the hair parameters,  
open synchronized dyeing in the hair dye window  
to see the final hair dye effect.  
You can also export the hair dye data created in the system  
as a USD file to use in other software.  
Go to the main menu,  
click File > Export,  
select the USD format,  
confirm the storage path,  
enter the file name,  
click Save,  
and then click Export in the USD window.  
Make sure the selection includes the hair dye data option  
so that the hair dye data is exported to the USD file.  
Here we show a section of the hair dye  
in the virtual engine,  
used to simulate a short video.  
In version 2025,  
the new hair dyeing material can be used to create the same hair dye  
in both the 3D window and the dyeing window.  
In addition,  
by exporting the hair dye data,  
you can import it into other tools  
and use it in various creative projects.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - Real-time Hair Generation
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Real-time Hair Generation in CLO 2025.0 This section explains the new real-time hair growth functionality introduced in CLO 2025.0, focusing on the Hair Growth Rate material, its real-time visualization in the 3D window, and compatibility improvements over previous versions. Since CLO 2025.0, users can directly create and view hair growth effects in the 3D window without the need for V-Ray rendering, which was the only option in earlier versions. This real-time capability simplifies the workflow significantly. The new Hair Growth Rate material type, added to the shell materials, replaces the previous method that required rendering for viewing hair effects. Moreover, unlike V-Ray-based hair rendering, which is only viewable within the rendering window and limits external application use, the Hair Growth Rate material can be exported in USD format. This improves compatibility with external tools and pipelines. Currently, this feature is exclusive to Windows systems, with Mac support planned for future releases. --- ## Displaying and Controlling Hair Growth Rate Material in the 3D Window This section details how to enable, visualize, and customize the Hair Growth Rate material in the CLO 3D window, including display options and hair appearance controls. To toggle the Hair Growth Rate material visibility in the 3D window: - Hover over the clothing rendering option in the switch menu. - Click the icon to display the Hair Growth Rate material. - The hair growth effect will appear directly on the fabric in real time. Users can assign random colors to the Hair Growth Rate material to differentiate hair growth patterns and inspect various hair shapes more easily. When using fabrics assigned the Hair Growth Rate material, other fabric-related options become disabled and cannot be selected. Hair appearance in the 3D window can be controlled via three different display modes accessible through **Settings > User Definition > 3D** under the Hair Growth Rate form: - **Original Hair:** Displays hair with both thickness and width, providing a realistic overall hair structure. - **Plane:** Displays hair with width but no thickness. - **Limit:** Displays hair as a simple curve with neither thickness nor width, useful for minimal visualization. The selected option sets the default hair display mode in the 3D view. --- ## Applying and Configuring Hair Growth Rate Material on Costumes This section explains the procedure to apply the Hair Growth Rate material to costume fabrics and customize hair parameters to create desired hairstyles. To apply the Hair Growth Rate material: 1. Select the fabric object (e.g., Fabric 1) in the Object window. 2. In the Attribute Editor, change the material type to **Hair Growth Rate**. 3. The hair will immediately display on the costume fabric in the 3D window. Users can select from various hair types available in the material settings. Similar to previous hair dye types, attribute details such as parameters, shape settings, and default application options can be adjusted at the bottom of the Attribute Editor to customize the hairstyle.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - Real-time Hair Generation
chunks.content: Select the fabric object (e.g., Fabric 1) in the Object window. 2. In the Attribute Editor, change the material type to **Hair Growth Rate**. 3. The hair will immediately display on the costume fabric in the 3D window. Users can select from various hair types available in the material settings. Similar to previous hair dye types, attribute details such as parameters, shape settings, and default application options can be adjusted at the bottom of the Attribute Editor to customize the hairstyle. Although Hair Growth Rate and hair dye share the same parameters and attribute settings, the hair distribution differs. A new **Random** option in the hair dye list allows users to modify the seed distribution value, creating different hair arrangements even with identical parameters. After adjusting hair parameters, enabling **Synchronized Dyeing** in the hair dye window synchronizes the hair dye effect with the hair growth material for consistent visualization. --- ## Exporting Hair Growth and Dye Data for External Use This section covers exporting hair growth and hair dye data in USD format for compatibility with other software and creative projects. Users can export hair dye data to USD files by following these steps: 1. Go to **File > Export** in the main menu. 2. Select the **USD** format. 3. Specify the storage path and file name. 4. Click **Save**, then **Export** in the USD export window. 5. Ensure the **Hair Dye Data** option is selected to include hair dye information in the USD file. The exported USD files containing hair growth and dye data can be imported into external tools and virtual engines for use in various projects, including animation and simulation. --- ## Summary of New Hair Dyeing Features in CLO 2025.0 This section highlights the unified hair dyeing workflow improvements and cross-application compatibility introduced in version 2025. CLO 2025.0 introduces a new hair dyeing material usable both in the 3D window and the hair dyeing window, enabling consistent hair color and style visualization across the interface. The addition of the Hair Growth Rate material combined with the ability to export hair dye data as USD files expands creative possibilities by allowing integration with external software and engines. This facilitates the use of CLO-generated hair styles and colors in broader workflows such as virtual production and game development.
